checkpoint.title: Checkpoint 4 — gate
checkpoint.prompt: Order the top layers (eval harness before skill compounding) and name the when-to-rebuild triggers.

lessons.title: The Eval Harness: Auto-Testing Every AI Run

facts.text: An **eval harness** is an automatic grader for AI work: it replays past sittings, lane by lane and class by class, and applies one gate — is a real, non-trivial deliverable present? Exit codes are ignored completely.

Why grade on artifacts? Because **exit 0 proves nothing** — verification was the layer everyone skipped by hand, so the tribunal ranked mechanizing it #1: read-only replay, low risk, and it would have caught both live defects.
Concrete case: replaying history flagged the **two oc-ds incidents**, where the lane exited 0 with an empty deliverable — and `hub eval <slug>` re-runs that exact check on demand today.
Common trap: **“it printed OK, so it worked.”** Under the harness, “no error” is never evidence — the only accepted proof is an artifact that exists and carries non-trivial content.

options: a lane can exit 0 with no deliverable

exercises.prompt: Why is the eval harness the #1 next layer?
options: it mechanizes the most-skipped layer (verification) and would've caught both defects

lessons.title: Quality Gates: Auto-Check Before You Ship

facts.text: **Verification gates** turn “trust me, it’s done” into machine-checked records: a sitting cannot close until exit status, deliverable presence, and a class probe have been recorded for every lane.

Why force records? Because sittings used to close on prose — a confident summary with nothing behind it. The phase’s own exit criterion says it plainly: at least one sitting must close **by gates, not prose**.
Concrete proof the gate bites: the acceptance test forces a failure, and that forced-failure sitting **cannot close without a gate record** — the check holds even when nobody is watching.
The **seam rule** keeps this honest over time: gate logic stays a small script, and past ~200 lines you stop and buy rather than grow it into a framework.

You are living the mechanic right now: this unit ends in a **gate-enforced checkpoint** — a graded verdict you must pass before the path continues, just as a sitting closes only through its gate record.

exercises.prompt: When does a sitting close under instrumented gates?
options: only after exit + presence + class probe are recorded
past ~200 lines of gate logic, stop and buy

exercises.prompt: The seam rule means verification gate logic should grow into a framework as it expands.

lessons.title: Skill Compounding: Turn Wins into Reusable Playbooks

facts.text: **Skill compounding** converts repeated wins into reusable playbooks: after enough validated runs of one class, the winning lanes’ deliverable structure is distilled into a playbook that future prompts receive automatically.
Why the waiting room? One lucky sitting teaches flukes, so distillation waits for **at least 3 validated sittings per class** — six same-day sittings is called out as overfitting territory.

The first playbook shipped live this way: the design-blueprint class distilled its winner’s structure at **75% (3 of 4 sittings)**, injected into future lane prompts — and verified present in the output.
Not every claim gets in: compounding reads **only `confidence=verified` plus `review_state=accepted`** records — a hard filter against baking unvalidated lessons into doctrine.
**Misconception:** capture lessons the moment they happen. Wrong lessons compound too — which is exactly why the eval harness is sequenced **before** compounding.

exercises.prompt: A playbook may be distilled only after:
Why is skill compounding sequenced AFTER the eval harness?

lessons.title: The Multica Test: Why We Evaluated It, What We Kept

facts.text: Any outside tool faces **named gates** before adoption — license, fit, effort — and the verdict ships either way. Multica failed the license gate: its custom terms forbid removing or modifying displayed branding without a written waiver, and the plan was to rebrand it outright.

A corrected license reading later opened the legal side (internal single-org use is fine; only displayed branding is protected) — and changed nothing, because the **architecture gate stood on its own**: a visible interactive board fights blind fanout, and always-on operation is a re-platform trigger with no workload.

The killer detail was verbatim: condition 1b covers UI code even when modified or extracted, and **“Multica now becomes the living tribunal” is precisely the act it forbids** — no waiver, no adoption.
What survived was **ideas, not code**: board-as-metaphor for the ledger, agents-as-teammates framing for the lane inventory, skills-as-playbooks — ideas are not copyrightable; UI and code are.

**Misconception:** “rejected means wasted effort.” The evaluation’s own recommendation — a thin static board built only after the data exists — is what actually got built, and the integration living in this workspace is labeled owner-confirmed-current: the evidence is the workspace itself.

options: reject as an adoption, on license AND architecture gates
adopt the tool, reject the ideas

lessons.title: When to Rebuild vs. When to Extend

facts.text: When do you throw away a working system and rebuild? The tribunal’s rule: **triggers are workload-shaped, not maturity-shaped** — you re-platform for load realities, never because a newer tool looks nicer.

Three triggers made the list: **concurrent mutation of the ledger** (locking or a database becomes unavoidable), **always-on event-driven operation** (a daemon, not cron), and a **crossed trust boundary** (multi-user, per-user auth).
Measured against the roadmap, none of the three is near — so the buy-verdict is **nothing**: adopting an orchestration framework now is re-platforming without a forcing trigger.

**Misconception:** “mature frameworks beat homegrown scripts — migrate early.” The ceiling review found files+CLI carries all six development items and the entire top-five layer list; the format tax is acknowledged but soft, not a wall.
One honest edge case: multi-round convergence is a DAG, not a fanout — at round three or more the tribunal should **delegate that sitting to a bought execution engine** instead of growing into one.

exercises.prompt: Which is a real re-platform trigger?

options: nothing — adopting now is re-platforming without a forcing trigger
